correctness.rationale: For q=r² the derivative numerator is N=q(w⁴+1)−4rc(w³+w)+(3+4qc²−q²)w²; the denominator V² is zero-free on the closed disk. Dividing N by w² gives the quadratic in u=w+w⁻¹ with discriminant 4q(1−q)(4c²−3−q). The boundary Poisson formula excludes u∈[−2,2] for either root; every other u has exactly one inverse in the disk, with nonzero local coordinate derivative. The conjugation relation and continuity of the real roots from the double root give precisely the stated nonreal-conjugate and real-sign regimes. At c=c₀, u₀=2c₀/r>2 and N=q(w²−u₀w+1)², with inner root t=(√(3+r²)−√(3(1−r²)))/(2r). Each base zero of C is simple because c∈(−1,1), so no critical value is zero; a shared value of two simple cubic critical points would require a fiber of degree at least four. Since C′(0)=q, the lift gives just the origin multiplicity n−1 and n copies of every nonzero ramification point with unchanged multiplicity (total 3n−1). For δ=c−c₀, N_{ww}=2q(u₀²−4)=6(1−q) and N_c=−8c₀(1−q)t² at the double root. Consequently F_w(c,t+x)=a(x²−bδ)+O_r(|x|³+|δx|+δ²), with a=3(1−q)/D₀² and b=8c₀t²/3. The reciprocal quadratic gives branch endpoints x=±√(bδ)+O_r(|δ|) on both sides. Integrating F_w between them gives −(4/3)a(bδ)^(3/2)+O_r(|δ|²) with a consistent square root; its absolute leading coefficient is exactly the stated K(r). Sign symmetry gives the other collision. This is local at fixed r, excludes the prescribed-zero collisions at c=±1, and applies also at n=1 where the origin is not critical. checker.py was inspected, not executed; the proof replaces finite splitting probes.
